t: You're at the WWT London Wetland Centre, a wetland reserve in Barnes, run by the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust. It's made from four disused Victorian reservoirs, tucked into a loop of the Thames beside Barn Elms. The man who founded it was Peter Scott, the ornithologist and conservationist. He was the only child of the Antarctic explorer Robert Falcon Scott, and he took an interest in wildfowl from a young age. He was also a painter, broadcaster and naval officer, so a wetland full of birds suits him well.
